prompt:
Use the attached original Ari character sheet as the sole character and style reference. Create ONE polished opaque landscape artist reference image with exactly TWO large, separate, whole-body illustrations of this same fictional adult Ari seated on the same simple armless wooden chair: straight FRONT view at left and genuine SIDE PROFILE facing PAGE LEFT at right. No standing view, portrait, inset or lettering. Leave generous margins around both heads, chair backs, chair bases, hands and shoes. Plain light neutral backdrop, a visible floor and soft clear lighting, appealing restrained stylized rendering consistent with the attached original. These are newly invented artist pose choices, not a technical rig or physical-fit demonstration.

Preserve Ari's warm medium-brown skin, full cheeks and soft jaw, readable eyes/brows, short tight dark curls, and the original broad soft rounded torso/middle/hips, substantial arms, thighs and calves. Keep the same approachable adult identity and calm attentive face, without a named expression or smile experiment. Do not slim or elongate the body, redesign the face/hair or add an accessory/prop.

Retain the matte rust short open bomber jacket, modest collar/cuffs/hem, slate crew-neck tee fully covering the abdomen/waist, roomy ink trousers and soft ivory low-top shoes. Keep the jacket fronts open around the covered middle; show the tee between the opening and trouser waist. Short jacket hem rests near hips without cutting through thigh/chair. Broad trouser thighs and knees retain room, with a few deliberate seated folds at hips/knees/hems instead of tight tubular legs. No exposed abdomen, pinched waist or unexplained garment holes.

Invent a plain unbranded armless chair with muted wood seat/back and four simple legs. Clothed hips visibly settle ON the seat, not floating in front of it. Chair back remains legible behind lower torso. Torso relaxed upright with slight forward inclination; thighs extend from hips forward to bent knees, lower legs reach shoes flat on floor. Chair feet and soles meet the same floor. Show the entire chair base. No chair arms obscuring anatomy.

FRONT: knees comfortably apart at roughly broad hip width, two clearly connected legs and both whole shoes visible. Ari's right hand (page LEFT in this front view) rests farther forward on its own knee. Ari's left hand (page RIGHT) rests higher/back on mid-thigh. Both open relaxed hands and sleeve-wrist connections visibly read; do not clasp/hide hands. Right foot sits farther forward, left foot nearer the chair, both flat and uncrossed.

SIDE PROFILE facing PAGE LEFT: nose, head, torso and chair arrangement read truly side-on, with face looking left and not turned toward viewer. The near hand rests on mid-thigh; the far hand rests distinctly farther forward on its own knee so both complete resting hands read without extra limbs or changing to a three-quarter camera. Near shin descends approximately vertically. Far shin angles forward; far shoe is farther left, with its heel just ahead of the near toe and a small visible floor gap, so both complete shoe silhouettes read while both feet remain flat and naturally connected to their own legs. Keep both shoes uncropped. Hips and far upper thigh may naturally overlap the nearer thigh/seat. Far aligned chair legs/back posts may partially hide behind near ones; don't invent extra chair legs to expose four. Keep the supported seated silhouette, broad body and covered clothing balance clear.

Prioritize one coherent seated character in each role, two arms/hands and two legs/feet each, plausible hip/seat and shoe/floor appearance, no detached or duplicated anatomy, floating soles, wrist-knee merges, contradictory pose or unexplained holes. Do not replace the required side profile with a three-quarter view. The goal is a useful original seated conversation target for an artist, retaining Ari's identity and clothing, with both required whole-body views legible together.
